results.correct_value: Mowich approach season: June to early July (the route's own window)
results.evidence: A park climbing-ranger report of a June 21-24 ascent states the route is typically climbed before the end of June and goes out of shape quickly once summer freezing levels rise, with rockfall and rotten snow below 11,500 ft. A separate route description says the route is often in good shape by May and that the old July opening of the Mowich road came after that. The 'July to mid-August' approach window only tracked the former Mowich road opening (no road exists since 2025) and sits after the climb's window, so it is aligned with the row's Jun-Jul season.

The only outside per-leg figures found (one trip-report author) give 3,100 + 3,300 ft to Thumb Rock and 3,600 ft from Thumb Rock to Columbia Crest via Liberty Cap, about 10,000 ft to the true summit, not to Liberty Cap. No source states a car-to-car gain ending at Liberty Cap, and computing one is not allowed. Settle with a published route figure for White River to Liberty Cap.

results.fact: Liberty Cap elevation (overview 14,097 vs summit pin and high_point_ft 14,112)
results.correct_value: 14,112 ft (published map elevation); recent GPS surveys of the melting icecap read ~14,095 ft
results.evidence: The encyclopedia article on Mount Rainier and a guide service's Liberty Ridge page both give Liberty Cap as 14,112 ft, matching high_point_ft and the summit pin. Independent GPS surveys (2025-2026, NAVD88) measure the thinning icecap at roughly 14,091-14,098 ft, so 14,097 is a recent survey reading, not the published elevation. The overview now gives the map figure and keeps the survey clause as a labelled aside.

results.fact: Whether Heliotrope Ridge can reach the X Couloir
results.correct_value: Heliotrope Ridge via the Thunder Glacier cirque is a valid (less direct) alternative approach to the southwest face; Rankin Creek from FR-38 is the more direct
results.evidence: The encyclopedia article says the southwest face is reached by following the Thunder Glacier cirque from the Heliotrope Ridge Trail, with the Middle Fork road as an alternative. A ski trip report says one could go in via Heliotrope but took the more direct FR-38; a second party chose Rankin Creek because it looked slightly shorter than the Heliotrope approach; and the Wilkes-Booth first-ascent party descended the southwest face route and walked out to the Heliotrope trailhead. The row's claim that Heliotrope serves only the NW face is removed in all four fields; the Coleman-cirque wrong-place warning and the camp-based descent warning are kept.
